why: Environment variables that redirect where a git command reads and writes. Git exports these into hooks, so a process that inherits one runs against a DIFFERENT repository than the one it appears to be standing in — which overwrote a shared branch with fixture commits more than once. Three copies of this list existed (the test harness, the worktree gate, the hook) and they had already drifted apart: review found the hook checking seven where the gate checked nine. One file owns it; every reader loads it.
failDirection: refuse — this is a DENYLIST, so a variable git adds later is not covered and fails toward permitting. That gap is why the repository-identity checks that read this list are not replaced by it.
